comments.author: slipperyp
comments.why: Documentary on Vipassana used as reform at a harsh Indian prison
comments.text: There is more information on the method from this documentary Doing Time, Doing Vipassana: [VIDEO] It documents the use of Vipassana as a reform measure at a harsh prison in India and traces the impacts it had on some of the inmates there.

comments.author: vekker
comments.story: What it’s like to spend four and a half years in solitary confinement (2015)
comments.why: Cited as support for teaching meditation in prisons
comments.text: Sounds like hell, the way he describes it. However, if you'd take those hellish elements away & ensure silence, I think long solitary confinement might work if you teach people how to meditate. That's just not being done enough in prisons right now. See "Doing Time, Doing Vipassana" [VIDEO] EDIT: I know this is probably a controversial opinion to non-meditators, but if you're going to downvote, at least provide an argument for why you don't agree.

comments.author: abledon
comments.story: California inmate takes unlikely path to freedom: podcasting
comments.why: Cited as example of mandatory meditation for prisoners
comments.text: mandatory meditation: [VIDEO] for someone to just 'sit' and think about their thoughts for 10 days straight without talking, is HELL for a criminal. they are forced to confront reality, or at least their subjective version of it.
